title_ne: आमाको दूधलाई प्रतिस्थापन गर्ने वस्तु (बिक्री वितरण नियन्‍त्रण) (पहिलो संशोधन) विधेयक, २०८३
summary:
The name of this bill is the Mother's Milk Substitutes (Control of Sale and Distribution) (First Amendment) Bill, 2083 (Section 1, Subsection 1, Page 1). This bill is brought to protect and promote breastfeeding, regulate the sale and distribution of infant foods including mother's milk substitutes to arrange safe and adequate nutrition for newborns and children, and amend the existing Act according to the present federal structure (Objectives and Reasons). This Act shall come into force immediately (Section 1, Subsection 2, Page 1).

The Government of Nepal may operate breastfeeding management centers or similar services to collect and manage mother's milk (Section 6, Page 3). The Ministry may make necessary standards to operate such services (Section 6, Page 3). Subject to the said standards, provincial governments, local levels, and other healthcare entities may operate breastfeeding management centers or similar services (Section 6, Page 3). For protecting and promoting breastfeeding, a Provincial Breastfeeding Protection and Promotion Committee shall exist in the province and a Local Breastfeeding Protection and Promotion Committee shall exist at the local level (Section 5, Page 2). The formation, functions, duties, and powers of these provincial and local committees shall be as determined by the concerned province and local level (Section 5, Page 2). On the recommendation of the Provincial Breastfeeding Protection and Promotion Committee, the provincial government, and on the recommendation of the Local Breastfeeding Protection and Promotion Committee, the local level may designate employees having specified qualifications as inspectors (Section 10, Subsection 2, Page 5). Until the provincial government and local level designate inspectors, the Ministry may designate inspectors for the province and local level as well on the recommendation of the Committee (Section 10, Subsection 2, Page 5).

Under these provisions, health workers, producers, distributors, healthcare entities, and shops or firms selling medicines are covered (Section 6, Section 7, Section 9, Page 3, 4). Health workers shall not recommend mother's milk substitutes or infant formula for feeding or using for children (Section 6, Page 3). However, health workers may recommend them if alternative breastfeeding is not possible when there is a risk of infection to the child from breastfeeding, the mother is severely ill and unconscious or unable to breastfeed, mother's milk is absent or insufficient, the mother is taking medication adverse to breastfeeding, the child has a severe health problem and cannot breastfeed, or the mother and child must remain separated for a long time (Section 6, Page 3). Unless approved by the Committee, producers or distributors shall not provide products to healthcare entities at a price lower than the retail price or donate them (Section 7, Subsection 2). Producers or distributors shall not engage in cross-promotion of mother's milk substitutes or products (Section 7, Subsection 4). Distributors shall not sell or distribute mother's milk substitutes or infant formula without a prescription from a health worker (Section 7, Subsection 4). Mother's milk substitutes or infant formula shall not be sold or distributed from anywhere other than shops or firms that have obtained certificates to sell medicines pursuant to prevailing law (Section 9). Deadlines applying to businesses and institutions are not stated in the bill.

It is provided that mother's milk substitutes or infant formula can only be sold or distributed from shops or firms that have obtained certificates to sell medicines pursuant to prevailing law (Section 9). Infant formula means a mother's milk substitute prepared in accordance with Nepali quality standards for the purpose of fulfilling the normal nutritional needs of children from birth up to three years of age (Section 2, Subsection 3, Page 1). The Ministry may make necessary standards to operate breastfeeding management centers or similar services (Section 6, Page 3). The word quality in the main Act has been updated to quality standard (Section 13, Page 7). Other specific provisions on licensing issuance or testing are not stated in the bill.

The bill provides for establishing a Provincial Breastfeeding Protection and Promotion Committee at the provincial level and a Local Breastfeeding Protection and Promotion Committee at the local level to protect and promote breastfeeding (Section 5, Page 2). In addition, the central Breastfeeding Protection and Promotion Committee is reconstituted, with the Secretary of the Ministry as Chairperson, and members including the Director General of the Department of Health Services, Joint Secretary of the Ministry looking after women and children, Director General of the Department of Commerce, Supplies and Consumer Protection, Director General of the Department of Food Technology and Quality Control, one pediatrician nominated by the Ministry, one nutrition expert nominated by the Ministry, Under Secretary (Law) of the Ministry, and the Director of the Family Welfare Division of the Department of Health Services as Member-Secretary (Section 3, Subsection 1, Page 1). The tenure of nominated members shall be two years and they may be re-nominated once, but persons involved in producing or selling and distributing mother's milk substitutes shall not be nominated (Section 3, Subsection 2, Page 2). The main functions of the committee include making necessary coordination with provincial and local committees and giving necessary directions to inspectors to protect, promote, and effectively regulate breastfeeding (Section 4, Subsection 1, Page 2; Section 10, Subsection 3, Page 5). The chief executive and fund of the committee are not stated in the bill.
